newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico global '16, '26 bonds seen good bet-Barings.
newsitem.headline: Mexico global '16, '26 bonds seen good bet-Barings.

text.p: Spreads on Mexico's outstanding sovereign '16 and '26 bonds are expected to narrow over similar term U.S. Treasuries, and should be overweight in portfolios, ING Barings said in a report on Tuesday.

Debt analyst Alex Krieckhaus said the Mexican sovereign yield curve, excluding Bradies, is steeper than the U.S. BB Industrial curve, with a differential of about 80 basis points at the short end of the curve and 150 basis points at the long end.
With the yield levels of Mexico's '16 and '26 bonds removed, both yield curves would be roughly parallel, he said.
As the spreads compress, the Mexican curve should flatten, he said.

"Specifically, we believe that in a three-month period the short-end could tighten about 20 basis points, whereas the long end could tighten 50 basis points in relation to the U.S. BB Industrial curve," Krieckhaus said.
"The long end seems likely to appreciate another 25 basis points over the rest of 1997," he said.
